fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is not presently a valid tensor amplification mechanism: a tensor product of affine cosets is not automatically a lattice coset whose nearest vectors are tensor powers of base nearest vectors. Mixed tensor-lattice vectors and variable gluing are uncontrolled, so the claimed rho^k shell law does not follow.

Proposal 3 would make satisfiability equivalent to exact membership of an explicitly constructed target in an integer boundary lattice. Since SNF decides that membership in polynomial time, the stated satisfiable-boundary versus unsatisfiable-nonzero-class mechanism cannot encode 3SAT unless some omitted nonlinearity, approximation condition, or superpolynomial construction carries the hardness.

Proposal 5 cannot simultaneously make several distinct legal one-hot labels zero-cost under one linear algebraic-integer detector while detecting every illegal affine combination in their span. Moreover, the product-formula lower bound applies to every nonzero legal displacement too, so the asserted O(m) completeness versus Omega(D) soundness accounting is unsupported.

Proposal 6 has a fatal asymptotic tradeoff: polynomial-size splitter families only handle suitably small sparsity thresholds, while deviations above a constant threshold have only constant selector norm and do not yield a polynomial gap over O(m) completeness energy. It also leaves modulo-q multiples and the existence of an honest-flow subtraction theorem unresolved.

Proposal 7's carry recurrence has no proved amplification law: a CVP witness may pay for the first nonzero recurrence residual and set later carries to zero, giving constant rather than geometric cost. Scaling recurrence rows would merely assume the amplification being sought, while exact global-detector kernel cheats remain untouched.

Proposal 4 factors through the same honest-relation quotient that Proposal 2 tests, but its q<10000, length-8 search cannot support the proposed h=m^(1+epsilon) barrier. Bose–Chowla separation before quotienting does not prevent honest cancellation constraints from identifying harmful columns, and modular q-multiple directions are unaccounted for.

Proposal 2 is the sole candidate worth one bounded prerequisite test, not a hardness result. Its global module, harmful affine set, polynomial-time relation generators, code map, full-rank CVP basis, target, and radius accounting are not yet specified, and finite survival on the eight-clause core would prove none of the required asymptotics.
evidence: The supplied slack verifier establishes only that the tested residual amplifier has exact squared optimum 27 versus Boolean baseline 19 because integer slack annihilates all amplified residuals. This directly forbids treating unanchored auxiliary coordinates as detected merely because residual evaluations are repeated.

The exact unbounded audit certifies 126 local harmful fibers empty over Q for the 18 fixed-marginal matrices. It supplies no evidence for any global quotient, overlap invariant, code, tensor shell, number-field shell, or polynomial amplification claim.

The overlap verifier reports a squared-norm-at-most-4 kernel move in every one of 5832 tested compositions and 95256 references. Thus no proposal may reuse the private-row local survivors or assume local isolation composes after unshared marginals are freed.
No verifier evidence supports any of the seven new mechanisms. The supplied records consistently state that no full CVP construction, hardness lemma, or dimension-dependent gap exists.

The previous provenance packet independently captures the overlap verifier but not the claimed standalone rerun output for the original survivor search. New experiments therefore require complete command output, generated artifacts, and independent hashes.
